title: Clip export reports every mistake with the file and clip it concerns
description:
As a beatmaker, I want every mistake in a clip export reported with the file and the clip it concerns, so that I can fix the manifest or the command instead of guessing.

Nothing is written for a sample that has an error; other samples in a folder export still export, and the command exits non-zero listing every problem.

```gherkin
Feature: Clip export reports every mistake with its location
  Scenario: A sample that was never analyzed
    Given the audio "new.wav" with no manifest
    When I export the clips of "new.wav"
    Then the export fails with "new.wav is not analyzed (no new.wav.apricity.json); run: python -m apricity_analyze.cli new.wav"

  Scenario: A manifest that breaks the schema names the place
    Given the manifest of "bad.wav" has "annotations.clips[2].end" set to "soon"
    When I export the clips of "bad.wav"
    Then the export fails with "bad.wav.apricity.json: /annotations/clips/2/end"

  Scenario: A clip past the end of the sample names the clip
    Given the ML clip "loop-3" of "short.wav" ends after the sample ends
    When I export the clips of "short.wav"
    Then the export fails with "short.wav.apricity.json: clip `loop-3` ends at 12.00 s, after the sample's end (10.00 s)"

  Scenario: Missing audio
    Given the manifest of "gone.wav" remains but the audio does not
    When I export the clips of "gone.wav"
    Then the export fails with "gone.wav: audio file not found"

  Scenario: An existing folder is not overwritten without --force
    Given the folder "Thunderer" exists
    When I export the clips of "Thunderer.wav"
    Then the export fails with "Thunderer exists; use --force to replace it"
    And the folder is unchanged

  Scenario: --force replaces the sample's folder, including clip files for markup that is gone
    Given the folder "Thunderer" holds "loops/A-4bars-Bb.alc" from an earlier export
    And the markup no longer has that loop
    When I export the clips of "Thunderer.wav" with "--force"
    Then "Thunderer/loops/A-4bars-Bb.alc" no longer exists

  Scenario: One bad sample does not stop the others
    Given the folder "marches" holds "a.wav" (analyzed) and "bad.wav" (whose manifest breaks the schema)
    When I export the clips of "marches"
    Then the folder "a" is written
    And the export fails listing "bad.wav.apricity.json"
```
